newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade seen slow on Monday.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade seen slow on Monday.

text.p: A standoff in the Plains cattle feedlot cattle market was expected on Monday with packers claiming they are under little pressure to buy and owners seeking higher prices, feedlot sources said.
"The packers are trying to tell us they have tremendous carryover and I find that hard to believe," one Oklahoma cattle feeder said.

Dealers said the key was if beef continued to move after the recent rise in prices to the highest level since December. In its closing report, USDA reported 150 fabricated loads of boxed beef sold on Friday, down from 263 loads a week earlier.

A small decline in the Texas showlist was expected next week, possibly of about 2,000 head to about 102,000. Feedlots sources said the level should start to fall more substantially in a couple of weeks time.
"In two more weeks we will be in the driving seat," one Oklahoma source said.
Kansas feedlot sources said the showlist should be between 90,000 and 95,000 head, versus about 95,000 head this week.
